# `silk/crypto/digest`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The interface of every streaming hash in `silk.crypto`, so generic code such as HMAC and PBKDF2
can take the hash as a type argument.

## When to use
Bound a type parameter with [`Digest`](#Digest) to write code that works with any hash, such as
`Hmac<H>` in `silk.crypto.hmac` or `Pbkdf2.derive<H>` in `silk.crypto.pbkdf2`. To hash data with
a known algorithm, call that hash's own functions, which return a fixed-size array.

## Details
MD5, SHA-1, the six SHA-2 hashes, the four SHA-3 hashes, and BLAKE2b-512 conform. Each state
is a fixed-size value that does not allocate. No block is longer than 144 bytes and no digest is
longer than 64 bytes, so generic code can keep them in arrays of those sizes.

## Examples
### Hash with any digest
```silk
import silk.crypto.digest { Digest }
import silk.crypto.sha2 { Sha256 }
import silk.crypto.sha1 { Sha1 }

fn firstByte<H: Digest>(message: &[u8]) -> u8 {
  let mut state: H = Digest.make()
  state.update(message)
  let mut digest: [u8; 64] = [0; 64]
  state.finishInto(&mut digest)
  return digest[0]
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // SHA-256("abc") starts with ba, and SHA-1("abc") with a9.
  if firstByte<Sha256>(b"abc") != 0xba || firstByte<Sha1>(b"abc") != 0xa9 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Digest` with `import silk.crypto.digest { Digest }`.

## `Digest`

```silk
pub interface Digest
```

A streaming hash: a state that takes a message in parts and returns a fixed-length digest.

### When to use

Bound a type parameter with it to write code that works with any hash of `silk.crypto`, such as
HMAC, PBKDF2, or a hash chosen by name at run time.

### Details

A provider is a fixed-size value that does not allocate. [`Digest.blockLength`](#Digest.blockLength) is at most 144
bytes and [`Digest.digestLength`](#Digest.digestLength) is at most 64 bytes for every provider in the standard
library.

<a id="Digest.make"></a>

### Operation `make`

```silk
fn make() -> Self
```

Returns a state for an empty message.

<a id="Digest.blockLength"></a>

### Operation `blockLength`

```silk
fn blockLength(self: &Self) -> usize
```

Returns the number of bytes the hash compresses at a time, such as 64 for SHA-256. HMAC pads
its key to this length.

<a id="Digest.digestLength"></a>

### Operation `digestLength`

```silk
fn digestLength(self: &Self) -> usize
```

Returns the number of bytes that [`Digest.finishInto`](#Digest.finishInto) writes, such as 32 for SHA-256.

<a id="Digest.objectIdentifier"></a>

### Operation `objectIdentifier`

```silk
fn objectIdentifier(self: &Self) -> &[u8]
```

Returns the content bytes of the DER object identifier that names the hash, without the tag
and length. Signature formats such as PKCS #1 v1.5 and X.509 name the hash with it.

<a id="Digest.update"></a>

### Operation `update`

```silk
fn update(self: &mut Self, bytes: &[u8]) -> ()
```

Adds `bytes` to the end of the message. Any split of the message gives the same digest.

<a id="Digest.copy"></a>

### Operation `copy`

```silk
fn copy(self: &Self) -> Self
```

Returns an independent copy of the state. Updates to either one do not change the other.

<a id="Digest.finishInto"></a>

### Operation `finishInto`

```silk
fn finishInto(self: Self, output: &mut [u8]) -> ()
```

Writes the digest of the message to the first [`Digest.digestLength`](#Digest.digestLength) bytes of `output` and
consumes the state. The bytes after them do not change. The program traps if `output` is
shorter.
